quests.question: She ordered ___ elegant three-course meal.
quests.hint: 'Elegant' begins with the vowel sound 'el'.
quests.explanation: Use 'an' before vowel sounds. 'Elegant' starts with the vowel 'e', so we write 'an elegant three-course meal'.

quests.question: I really enjoyed ___ lunch they prepared for us.
quests.sentence: I really enjoyed ___ lunch they prepared for us.
quests.hint: The specific lunch already prepared - we know which one.
quests.explanation: Use 'the' when referring to a specific meal or event that is already known. 'The lunch they prepared' identifies this particular meal.

quests.question: They speak ___ English very fluently.
quests.hint: Language names alone - without 'language' - take no article.
quests.explanation: When a language name is used alone, no article is needed: 'She speaks French', 'He studies Mandarin', 'They read Arabic'. Use 'the' only when 'language' follows: 'the English language'.

quests.question: They prepared ___ quick meal before the game.
quests.sentence: They prepared ___ quick meal before the game.
quests.hint: 'Quick' begins with the consonant sound 'kw'.
quests.explanation: Use 'a' before consonant sounds. 'Quick' starts with 'qu' (pronounced 'kw'), so we write 'a quick meal'.

quests.question: ___ English language is spoken on every continent.
quests.sentence: ___ English language is spoken on every continent.
quests.hint: When 'language' follows the language name, use 'the'.
quests.explanation: The pattern '[Language name] + language' always uses 'the': the English language, the French language, the Spanish language. Without 'language', no article is used.

quests.question: We usually have ___ breakfast at seven.
quests.sentence: We usually have ___ breakfast at seven.
quests.hint: Meal names used in a routine context take no article.
quests.explanation: Meal names (breakfast, lunch, dinner, supper) in general statements about habits or routines take no article: 'We have breakfast at seven', 'She skips lunch', 'They serve dinner at eight'.

quests.question: He wanted ___ ice-cold lemonade.
quests.hint: 'Ice-cold' begins with the vowel sound 'eye'.
quests.explanation: Use 'an' before vowel sounds. 'Ice-cold' starts with the vowel 'i' (pronounced 'eye'), so we write 'an ice-cold lemonade'.

quests.question: He watched ___ game last night.
quests.hint: The specific game discussed - both speakers know which one.
quests.explanation: Use 'the' when referring to a specific event that both the speaker and listener already know about. 'The game' means the particular match they have been discussing.

quests.question: She plays ___ tennis every morning.
quests.hint: Sports and games take no article.
quests.explanation: Sports names take no article when used generally: 'She plays tennis', 'He loves football', 'They practice basketball'. Exception: musical instruments use 'the' - 'She plays the piano'.

quests.question: It was ___ delicious vegetarian dish.
quests.hint: 'Delicious' begins with the consonant sound 'd'.
quests.explanation: Use 'a' before consonant sounds. 'Delicious' starts with 'd', so we write 'a delicious vegetarian dish'.

quests.question: ___ French they speak has a Parisian accent.
quests.sentence: ___ French they speak has a Parisian accent.
quests.hint: The specific variety of French they speak - defined by context.
quests.explanation: When a language refers to a specific variety spoken by specific people, use 'the': 'The French they speak is very formal.' Compare: 'She speaks French' (general, no article).

quests.question: He studied ___ Spanish at university.
quests.hint: Language name alone, without 'language', takes no article.
quests.explanation: Language names used alone take no article: 'He studied Spanish', 'She learned Mandarin', 'They teach Arabic'. Add 'the' only when 'language' follows: 'the Spanish language'.

quests.question: She played ___ intense match.
quests.hint: 'Intense' begins with the vowel sound 'in'.
quests.explanation: Use 'an' before vowel sounds. 'Intense' starts with the vowel 'i', so we write 'an intense match'.

quests.question: They won ___ final match of the season.
quests.sentence: They won ___ final match of the season.
quests.hint: The specific final match - there is only one final match.
quests.explanation: Use 'the' with 'final', 'first', 'last', and ordinal words, as they identify a unique event: the final match, the first game, the last round.

quests.question: They serve ___ dinner at eight o'clock.
quests.sentence: They serve ___ dinner at eight o'clock.
quests.hint: Meal names in general routine statements take no article.
quests.explanation: Meal names in habitual or routine contexts take no article: 'They serve dinner at eight', 'We have lunch at noon', 'She cooks breakfast on weekends'.

quests.question: He joined ___ local football club.
quests.hint: 'Local' begins with the consonant sound 'l'.
quests.explanation: Use 'a' before consonant sounds. 'Local' starts with 'l', so we write 'a local football club'.

quests.question: ___ breakfast at the hotel is included in the price.
quests.sentence: ___ breakfast at the hotel is included in the price.
quests.hint: The specific breakfast served at this specific hotel.
quests.explanation: Use 'the' when a meal refers to a specific, identifiable one. 'The breakfast at the hotel' means the particular breakfast meal served at that hotel.

quests.question: I enjoy playing ___ chess.
quests.hint: Board games and sports take no article.
quests.explanation: Board games and sports take no article when used generally: 'She plays chess', 'He loves poker', 'They enjoy tennis'. Compare: 'She plays the piano' (the, for instruments).

quests.question: This is ___ English grammar book.
quests.hint: 'English' begins with the vowel sound 'en'.
quests.explanation: Use 'an' before vowel sounds. 'English' starts with the vowel 'e', so we write 'an English grammar book'.

quests.question: She plays ___ piano beautifully.
quests.hint: Musical instruments use 'the' when you mean playing the instrument as a skill.
quests.explanation: In English, we use 'the' before musical instruments: 'She plays the piano', 'He plays the guitar', 'She practices the violin'. This is a fixed grammatical pattern.

quests.question: She teaches ___ Russian at the language school.
quests.sentence: She teaches ___ Russian at the language school.
quests.hint: Language name alone takes no article.
quests.explanation: Language names without 'language' take no article: 'She teaches Russian', 'He studies Arabic', 'They learn Mandarin'.

quests.question: They built ___ sports arena nearby.
quests.hint: 'Sports' begins with the consonant sound 's'.
quests.explanation: Use 'a' before consonant sounds. 'Sports' starts with 's', so we write 'a sports arena'.

quests.question: They are translating ___ ancient manuscript.
quests.hint: The specific manuscript they are working on - we know which one.
quests.explanation: Use 'the' to refer to a specific, known item. 'The ancient manuscript' refers to the particular text they have been assigned to translate.

quests.question: We love having ___ lunch outdoors.
quests.hint: Meal names in a general preference statement take no article.
quests.explanation: Meal names in general statements about preferences or habits take no article: 'I love lunch outdoors', 'We enjoy breakfast together', 'He prefers dinner early'.

quests.question: She wants ___ orange juice.
quests.hint: 'Orange' begins with the vowel sound 'or'.
quests.explanation: Use 'an' before vowel sounds. 'Orange' starts with the vowel 'o', so we write 'an orange juice'.

quests.question: ___ dinner last night was outstanding.
quests.hint: The specific dinner that happened last night - a known event.
quests.explanation: Use 'the' to refer to a specific meal that has already taken place. 'The dinner last night' identifies one particular meal.

quests.question: They practice ___ soccer after school.
quests.hint: Sport names used in a general routine context take no article.
quests.explanation: Sports take no article when used generally: 'They practice soccer', 'She plays volleyball', 'He runs track'. No article is needed.

quests.question: It was ___ long and exciting game.
quests.sentence: It was ___ long and exciting game.
quests.hint: 'Long' begins with the consonant sound 'l'.
quests.explanation: Use 'a' before consonant sounds. 'Long' starts with 'l', so we write 'a long and exciting game'.

quests.question: They supported ___ local team.
quests.hint: The specific local team - both speakers know which one they mean.
quests.explanation: Use 'the' when referring to a specific, known team. 'The local team' is the particular team from their area that both speakers recognize.

quests.question: He plays ___ golf every weekend.
quests.hint: Golf is a sport - sports take no article.
quests.explanation: Sports and games take no article when used generally: 'He plays golf', 'She surfs', 'They play cricket'. Exception: 'She plays the piano' (musical instruments use 'the').
